who: Charles F. Robinson II, historian of the American South at the University of Arkansas; history PhD, University of Houston.

evidence.says: Scott A. Cashion’s May 2013 history dissertation lists Robinson, Charles F. II as advisor.
Connects Charles F. (Charles Frank) Robinson with The antimiscegenation conversation (May 1998) and Dangerous liaisons, naming Charles Frank Robinson II.
Lists Houston PhD graduate Charles Robinson II, author of The Antimiscegenation Conversation, as an Arkansas associate professor.

notes: The student, full name, dissertation and Arkansas appointment identify p-121287. Charles M. Robinson is a different author.

who: Mario Rodríguez, historian of Central America at the University of Southern California; history PhD, Berkeley, 1952.

evidence.says: The February 2005 scholarly newsletter identifies Rodríguez as a Central American historian, gives his Berkeley history doctorate in 1952, lists Southern California among his appointments, and names A Palmerstonian Diplomat in Central America.
Identifies Mario Rodríguez as the author of A Palmerstonian diplomat in Central America (1964).
A May 1982 professional report identifies Mario Rodríguez of the University of Southern California chairing a session on Spanish American independence.

notes: The doctorate matches exactly; the contemporary USC affiliation and the authority-linked book establish the candidate identity.

who: Nancy Lyman Roelker, historian of sixteenth-century France and mentor of Brown graduate students; Harvard PhD, 1953.

evidence.says: Brown’s finding aid identifies Kristen B. Neuschel as a Brown PhD of 1982 and records Roelker’s statement that she directed Neuschel.
Identifies Nancy Lyman Roelker, her research on sixteenth-century France, Brown teaching materials, and a Harvard PhD in 1953.
Expands Nancy L. Roelker to Nancy Lyman Roelker and records a Harvard PhD in 1953.

notes: Direct evidence of the named student confirms the match. The supplied Radcliffe 1952 doctorate differs from the Brown finding aid and LC record, which say Harvard 1953.

who: Jessica Choppin Roney, historian of early America at Temple University since 2014; PhD, Johns Hopkins University.

evidence.says: Identifies Jessica Choppin Roney as Temple history faculty since 2014, with a Johns Hopkins PhD and the book Governed by a Spirit of Opposition.
Alexandra L. Straub’s May 2020 dissertation Making Water Pure names Jessica Roney as advisory chair in History.
Expands Jessica C. Roney to Jessica Choppin Roney and identifies her as author of Governed by a spirit of opposition (2014).

notes: The expanded name, book, doctorate institution and named student agree.

who: Robert A. Schneider, historian of early modern France; Catholic University faculty, 1990–2005, then Indiana University; PhD, Michigan.

evidence.says: Lists Webster G. Tarpley’s Paolo Sarpi dissertation under 2008–2009, directed by Robert A. Schneider.
Gives a Michigan PhD, Catholic University appointments in 1990–2005, Indiana appointment from 2005, and Tarpley among completed dissertations supervised.
Links Robert Alan Schneider to the usage Robert A. Schneider, Public life in Toulouse, The ceremonial city, and Indiana University history faculty from 2005.

notes: The university explicitly confirms supervision after his move to Indiana. The authority record and CV identify the same author.

who: Rebecca Shumway, historian of West Africa and the Atlantic world at Wisconsin–Milwaukee; history PhD, Emory, 2004.

evidence.says: Identifies Shumway as a Wisconsin–Milwaukee history associate professor with an Emory history PhD in 2004.
Her March 2025 institutional CV gives Milwaukee employment from August 2019, Pittsburgh employment in 2006–2013, and The Fante and the Transatlantic Slave Trade (2011).
Identifies Rebecca Shumway, author of The Fante and the transatlantic slave trade (2011), as a Pittsburgh history assistant professor.
The department’s June 2025 graduation notice captions a photograph of Kitonga Alexander with Rebecca Shumway.

notes: The exact doctorate, career sequence and authority-linked book establish the match; the graduation notice also connects the named student.

The spring 2023 program pairs doctoral graduate Meredith K. Stukey with Michael G. Smith.
